Subject: High tail latency and 5xx spike during afternoon peak

Hi Vivek —

We're seeing a large increase in long-tail completion latency (p99-99.9) and a correlated surge in 5xx errors starting ~13:50 PDT today. This started shortly after we rolled the new prompt-layer optimization (same config we've used for the last month). Impact: user-facing timeouts and degraded throughput.

Symptom summary:
- p95 ~ 300ms (normal) but p99 jumped from ~1.2s to 6–12s, and p99.9 samples show repeated 30–45s completions that then 500.
- Error rate (5xx) spiked from 0.2% to ~4% between 13:50–15:30
- Throughput drop: sustained 20% reduction in successful completions during the window

We captured sample traces and some raw server-side timing logs (attached: packetly_tail_samples.txt). We also put a folder in Drive with traces: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Packetly-Incident-Logs

Can you advise next steps? This is customer-impacting and we need immediate help — any temporary mitigations we can apply while you investigate root cause?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: High tail latency and 5xx spike during afternoon peak

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed a sudden rise in queued request depth on the customer shard (shard-id: pk-71a) starting 13:48 PDT. Queue depth correlates with the p99 spike.
- Telemetry shows adaptive batching increased average batch sizes ~2.3x at the start of the window — likely due to a small number of long requests inflating batch aggregation windows.
- Concurrently, the per-worker concurrency cap (configured at 32) hit hard on 3 workers, causing request queuing and then circuit-breaker induced 5xx when queue timeout was reached.
- KV cache miss rate increased by ~15% in the same window (more cold starts), which can magnify completion times.

Proposed short-term mitigations (apply now):
1) Reduce max batch size from 64 -> 16 for the customer shard for 30 minutes — should lower batching-induced jitter.
2) Temporarily raise per-worker concurrency cap from 32 -> 48 on two spare workers (if infra/ops approves) to relieve backpressure while we root cause.
3) Enable prefix/KV prefetch for their hottest keys to reduce cache miss amplification.

I can push the batch-size override immediately (no deploy) and run a canary to verify impact. I'll also attach a short sample of the tail latencies and the trace bundle to our ticket.

Marissa
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
